phase: Phase 1 — debug/QA surface (player-facing UI is Phase 2, out of scope)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A pure tag-derivation pass turns a generated systemData into a tag set: isBinary, primary/secondary spectral type, planetCount, hasRings, hasHabitable, archetype.

verifyVia.input: Call deriveSystemTags(systemData) on known fixtures (e.g. Sol via KnownSystems, a seeded binary, a seeded ringed-giant system).
verifyVia.observable: Returned tags match the fixture's actual contents — Sol: not binary, planetCount=8, hasHabitable=true; a binary fixture: isBinary=true with both star types; a ringed fixture: hasRings=true.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A cheap fast-path derives the early tags (isBinary, spectral type(s), planetCount, archetype) WITHOUT running the per-planet loop, and never perturbs the full generator's RNG draw order.

verifyVia.input: Call the cheap derivation for a seed+galaxyContext; separately call full StarSystemGenerator.generate(seed, ctx).
verifyVia.observable: Cheap tags equal the full-generation values for those same fields; PlanetGenerator.generate is not invoked by the cheap path (spy/instrument); and a full generate(seed) before vs. after a cheap call produces an identical system (RNG order preserved).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A probe aimed at an arbitrary galactic region (prism/cube/radius via HashGridStarfield) sweeps that volume and returns systems matching a cheap-tag filter, deterministically.

verifyVia.input: Run a probe at a fixed center+volume with a cheap filter (e.g. isBinary=true), twice.
verifyVia.observable: Both runs return the identical result list; every result lies within the requested volume and matches the filter; each result carries a navStarData snapshot + its tags.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Selectable scan depth: a 'deep' scan cheap-filters the region then fully generates the survivors to confirm expensive tags (hasRings, hasHabitable); 'shallow' does not.

verifyVia.input: Run the same probe+region with a hasRings filter at scan depth 'shallow' vs 'deep'.
verifyVia.observable: Deep results contain only systems whose full generation confirms a ringed planet (verified by re-generating and scanning planets[]); shallow returns the cheap-tag candidate set (a superset or proxy), and the two result sets differ as expected for that mode.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Saving the current system writes a navStarData snapshot ({worldX,worldY,worldZ,seed,type}) + derived tags to a persisted store that survives a page reload.

verifyVia.input: Invoke 'save current system' while in a system, then reload the page and read the saved-systems store.
verifyVia.observable: After reload, the store contains an entry with the system's navStarData + tags; the snapshot fields are non-empty and match the system that was active when saved.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Selecting a saved entry reproduces the IDENTICAL system via the existing Priority-1 navStarData warp path — not a near-miss.

verifyVia.input: Save a system, then reload it from the saved entry by feeding its navStarData back through the warp resolution path.
verifyVia.observable: The regenerated systemData deep-equals the original on identity fields: same seed, same star.type/star2.type, same planetCount, same per-planet types and rings (determinism proof).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The persisted saved-systems list is itself filterable by tag.

verifyVia.input: Populate the saved list with mixed systems, then filter by a tag (e.g. hasHabitable=true).
verifyVia.observable: Only the saved entries whose tags match the filter are returned.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max, with his hands in the debug panel, can see the current system's tags, save it, aim a probe at a region, run a tag-search, and warp to a result.

verifyVia.input: Max opens the debug panel in the running game, reads the current system's tags, clicks save, opens the probe, sets a region + tag filter, runs the search, and selects a result to warp to.
verifyVia.observable: He sees the tags rendered; the saved entry appears; the probe returns a matching list; selecting a result warps him into that system — all without console errors.

inputs: HashGridStarfield.findStarsInPrism / findStarsInCube / findStarsInRadius (region sweep over arbitrary center coords)
StarSystemGenerator.generate / generateAsync and its _generateIterator (full system; basis for the cheap fast-path)
GalacticMap.deriveGalaxyContext(position) — pure position->context (metallicity, age, starWeights, features)
navStarData shape {worldX,worldY,worldZ,seed,type} and the Priority-1 warp resolution path (main.js ~2920)
PlanetGenerator (rings @520, habitabilityScore @571) — the source of the expensive tags for deep scan
outputs: DebugPanel.js — new controls: show current-system tags, save system, probe region + scan-depth + tag filter, jump-to-result
a persisted saved-systems store (localStorage) keyed by navStarData snapshot + tags
deriveSystemTags() + cheap-tag API — the seam a Phase 2 player-facing share UI will consume
mustStayWorking: StarSystemGenerator determinism: same seed+galaxyContext -> identical system. The cheap fast-path MUST be read-only / replay the exact early Alea draws and must not change the full generator's draw order (Alea is sequential; out-of-order consumption changes everything downstream).
Existing warp resolution Priority 1 (navStarData) and Priority 2 (starIndex) — unchanged behavior
KnownSystems.findAt overrides (Sol etc.) still take precedence at their positions
spawnWithSeed debug path continues to work (it is the lossy bare-seed path; not the save/reload path)
